deductions: The overall dance phrase is preserved: same side-to-side swaying, bent raised arm, opposite palm-out gestures, wide-legged stepping, and recurring lean-back poses across the sampled frames.

Several sampled poses are close but not exact: B is often a little more upright with straighter legs where A has deeper crouches or stronger hip/torso lean, especially around row 1 columns 2-4, row 2 columns 2-4, and row 5 column 6.
Some arm/hand timing differs slightly: B's palms and wrists are more open/extended in a few frames while A's hands are more compact or fist-like.
Jacket-flare moments broadly match but are not always at the same intensity or position, e.g. the stronger coat swing in A around row 2 column 1 and row 4 column 3 is softer/different in B.
B keeps the main wardrobe concept: shiny dark oversized suit, white shirt, black belt/shoes, and loose tie/suspender-like dark lines.
The suit in B appears more gray/silver and less uniformly black-glossy than A.
B's shirt collar/tie area looks more open and disheveled, with the tie or neckwear less like A's centered tie in several frames.
B's trousers sometimes look straighter and less ballooned/pleated than A's very baggy retro pants.
Both use a plain white studio/background with no added set elements.
B shows a slightly more visible floor plane and soft shadowing, while A looks flatter/cleaner white with a more cut-out or keyed appearance.
Both are full-body, front-facing, centered dance shots with very similar scale.
B has a slightly more grounded studio framing with visible floor/shadow, whereas A appears more floating/composited on a flat white field.
There are small differences in body scale and vertical placement across frames, but no major crop or camera-angle mismatch.
B retains the low-budget white-background dance-video style and shiny suit aesthetic.
B looks somewhat cleaner and more modern/realistic, especially because of the floor shadow and more natural studio lighting.
A has a stronger retro composited/flat-white keyed look.
B's face, hair, and facial hair differ from A, but this is treated as allowed identity personalization.
No major deduction applied for facial identity differences.

overall.summary: B is a strong regeneration of A: same scene type, costume concept, framing, and most choreography beats. It is not nearly perfect because the body posing/timing has repeated small mismatches, the suit/tie details differ, and B has a cleaner grounded studio look instead of A's flatter retro keyed look.

uncertainty_due_to_sampled_frames.explanation: The comparison is based on 30 sampled frames at 1/6-second intervals, so between-frame motion, exact timing, and transitions may differ more or less than visible here.
